event.question: What changed in the EU AI Act obligations for general-purpose AI models this year?

event.thought: Decision log: The question asks about 2026 changes to EU AI Act obligations for general-purpose AI (GPAI) models. Key context: GPAI obligations became applicable Aug 2, 2025, with the GPAI Code of Practice and Commission guidelines emerging around then — so 2026 changes likely involve enforcement powers activating, Code of Practice adoption/signatories, and any amendments or delays. I'll spend both my researchers now in parallel: one on the regulatory timeline/enforcement milestones hitting in 2026, and one on the Code of Practice, guidelines, and any proposed amendments or simplification ("digital omnibus"). This maximizes coverage since my budget is tight.

event.title: GPAI obligations timeline and enforcement in 2026
event.summary: On August 2, 2026, the EU AI Office gained active enforcement powers over GPAI providers, including authority to request documentation, conduct evaluations, demand remedial measures, restrict/withdraw models, and impose fines up to 3% of global annual turnover or €15 million. GPAI obligations themselves had applied since August 2, 2025, but enforcement was deferred one year. Models placed on market before August 2, 2025 have until August 2, 2027 to comply. Stop-the-clock proposals were rejected, but the Digital Omnibus delayed high-risk system deadlines while leaving GPAI timelines unchanged.

event.title: GPAI Code of Practice, guidelines, and digital omnibus simplification
event.summary: The final GPAI Code of Practice (published July 10, 2025) comprises three chapters on transparency, copyright, and safety-security with 26 signatories including Amazon, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI. The Commission's July 18, 2025 guidelines define GPAI as models trained on >10²³ FLOPs with general capabilities. A mandatory training data summary template became effective August 2, 2025, with compliance enforcement starting August 2, 2026. The Digital Omnibus (Regulation 2026/1744, entered force July 27, 2026) leaves core GPAI obligations (Articles 51-55) unchanged but postpones Article 50(2) synthetic content transparency marking to December 2, 2026, while maintaining systemic risk thresholds at 10²⁵ FLOPs.

event.report_md:
## TL;DR
- The headline 2026 change is **enforcement, not new rules**: as of **August 2, 2026** the EU AI Office gained active powers over general-purpose AI (GPAI) providers, one year after the obligations themselves took effect [1].
- The AI Office can now request documentation, run technical evaluations, demand risk-mitigation, and restrict or withdraw models, backed by fines up to **3% of global turnover or €15 million** [1][4].
- The **Digital Omnibus** (Regulation 2026/1744, in force July 27, 2026) delayed high-risk-system deadlines but left core GPAI obligations (Articles 51–55) untouched [3][9].
- Transparency labeling under **Article 50** activates in 2026, with machine-readable marking of AI-generated content pushed to **December 2, 2026** [2][9].

## From obligations to enforcement
GPAI obligations under the AI Act have applied since **August 2, 2025**, but enforcement was deliberately deferred by one year to give providers an adjustment period [1]. That period ended on **August 2, 2026**, when the Commission/AI Office's supervisory and enforcement powers became active [1]. From that date the AI Office can request documentation, conduct evaluations, require corrective measures, and restrict or withdraw non-compliant models, with fines up to 3% of annual worldwide turnover or €15 million, whichever is higher [1]. Notably, refusing or delaying compliance with these requests is itself a finable offense [4]. Models placed on the market **before** August 2, 2025 get extra time — compliance is required only by **August 2, 2027** [1][7].

## Code of Practice, guidelines, and data transparency
The framework providers rely on was set in mid-2025 and became operative into 2026. The final **GPAI Code of Practice** was published July 10, 2025, with three chapters (transparency, copyright, safety-security) and 26 signatories including Amazon, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI [5]. The Commission's **July 18, 2025 guidelines** defined a GPAI model as one trained using more than **10²³ FLOPs** with general generative capabilities [6]. A mandatory **training-data summary template** — covering six data categories from public datasets to scraped and synthetic data — became effective August 2, 2025; enforcement and corrective measures on it begin August 2, 2026, and pre-2025 models have until August 2, 2027 [7][8].

## What the Digital Omnibus did (and did not) change
The **Digital Omnibus** (Regulation 2026/1744, entered into force July 27, 2026) was the year's main legislative adjustment. A broader "Stop-the-Clock" moratorium was rejected [3]. The Omnibus postponed high-risk-system deadlines (to December 2027 and August 2028) but **left GPAI obligations under Articles 51–55/56 unchanged** [3][9][10]. Systemic-risk thresholds remain at **10²⁵ FLOPs**, and documentation, copyright-policy, and serious-incident-reporting duties continue under the original framework [10]. The one GPAI-adjacent timing tweak: Article 50(2) machine-readable marking of synthetic content moved from August 2 to **December 2, 2026** [9].

## Open questions
- How aggressively will the AI Office use its new enforcement powers in its first months, and against whom [1][4]?
- How will pre-August-2025 models be treated in the 2026–2027 transition window in practice [1][7]?
- Will future Digital Omnibus iterations revisit GPAI systemic-risk thresholds or duties [9][10]?
